question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\sqrt{2}),$ calculate $P(X>\sqrt{2}).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.

current_example.problem: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(\dfrac 23\right),$ calculate $P\left(X \geq 3\right).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
current_example.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14129107/assets/74e7942eac1d5b8c66c2cb0b1ee5886981b328fefde6064fcc669f7fd655af55.svg)

We're given that

$$
X\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( \dfrac 23 \right).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14129107/assets/c7e88f4185cac7ba3aa027a4450aa032b1364db7cfdcf964ee11b78ed4599d6b.svg)Therefore, we can calculate $P\left(X \geq 3\right)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3) & ={\int }_{3}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{2}{3}{e}^{-2x/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{{e}^{-2x/3}|}_{3}^{\infty } \\  & ={e}^{-2} \\  & ≈0.1353\end{aligned}
$$
